name: apropos
desc: Help Apropos. Prompt the user for a string, open the *help* buffer, and list all commands that contain that string.

name: audible-bell
desc: Toggle the audible system bell.

name: auto-execute
desc: Register an auto-execute hook; that is, specify a filename pattern (conforming to the shell's filename globbing rules) and an associated function to execute when a file matching the specified pattern is read into a buffer.

name: auto-fill-mode
desc: Toggle auto-fill mode (sometimes called mail-mode) in the current buffer, where text inserted past the fill column is automatically wrapped to a new line. Can be set globally with set-default-mode .

name: auto-indent-mode
desc: Toggle indent mode in the current buffer, where indentation is preserved after a newline. Can be set globally with set-default-mode .

name: back-to-indentation
desc: Move the dot to the first non-whitespace character on the current line.

name: backup-to-home-directory
desc: Save backup copies to a ~/.mg.d directory instead of working directory. Requires make-backup-files to be on.

name: backward-char
desc: Move cursor backwards one character.

name: backward-kill-word
desc: Kill text backwards by n words.

name: backward-paragraph
desc: Move cursor backwards n paragraphs. Paragraphs are delimited by <NL><NL> or <NL><TAB> or <NL><SPACE>.

name: backward-word
desc: Move cursor backwards by the specified number of words.

name: beginning-of-buffer
desc: Move cursor to the top of the buffer. If set, keep mark's position, otherwise set at current position. A numeric argument n will move n/10th of the way from the top.

name: beginning-of-line
desc: Move cursor to the beginning of the line.

name: blink-and-insert
desc: Self-insert a character, then search backwards and blink its matching delimiter. For delimiters other than parenthesis, brackets, and braces, the character itself is used as its own match. Can be used in the startup file with the global-set-key command.

name: bsmap-mode
desc: Toggle bsmap mode, where DEL and C-h are swapped.

name: c-mode
desc: Toggle a KNF-compliant mode for editing C program files.

name: call-last-kbd-macro
desc: Invoke the keyboard macro.

name: capitalize-word
desc: Capitalize n words; i.e. convert the first character of the word to upper case, and subsequent letters to lower case.

name: cd
desc: Change the global working directory. See also global-wd-mode .

name: column-number-mode
desc: Toggle whether the column number is displayed in the modeline.

name: copy-region-as-kill
desc: Copy all of the characters in the region to the kill buffer, clearing the mark afterwards. This is a bit like a kill-region followed by a yank .

name: count-matches
desc: Count the number of lines matching the supplied regular expression.

name: count-non-matches
desc: Count the number of lines not matching the supplied regular expression.

name: cscope-find-this-symbol
desc: List the matches for the given symbol.

name: cscope-find-global-definition
desc: List global definitions for the given literal.

name: cscope-find-called-functions
desc: List functions called from the given function.

name: cscope-find-functions-calling-this-function
desc: List functions calling the given function.

name: cscope-find-this-text-string
desc: List locations matching the given text string.

name: cscope-find-egrep-pattern
desc: List locations matching the given extended regular expression pattern.

name: cscope-find-this-file
desc: List filenames matching the given filename.

name: cscope-find-files-including-file
desc: List files that #include the given filename.

name: cscope-next-symbol
desc: Navigate to the next match.

name: cscope-prev-symbol
desc: Navigate to the previous match.

name: cscope-next-file
desc: Navigate to the next file.

name: cscope-prev-file
desc: Navigate to the previous file.

name: cscope-create-list-of-files-to-index
desc: Create cscope's List and Index in the given directory.

name: define-key
desc: Prompts the user for a named keymap (mode), a key, and an command, then creates a keybinding in the appropriate map.

name: delete-backward-char
desc: Delete backwards n characters. Like delete-char , this actually does a kill if presented with an argument.

name: delete-blank-lines
desc: Delete blank lines around dot. If dot is sitting on a blank line, this command deletes all the blank lines above and below the current line. Otherwise, it deletes all of the blank lines after the current line.

name: delete-char
desc: Delete n characters forward. If any argument is present, it kills rather than deletes, saving the result in the kill buffer.

name: delete-horizontal-space
desc: Delete any whitespace around the dot.

name: delete-leading-space
desc: Delete leading whitespace on the current line.

name: delete-trailing-space
desc: Delete trailing whitespace on the current line.

name: delete-matching-lines
desc: Delete all lines after dot that contain a string matching the supplied regular expression.

name: delete-non-matching-lines
desc: Delete all lines after dot that don't contain a string matching the supplied regular expression.

name: delete-other-windows
desc: Make the current window the only window visible on the screen.

name: delete-window
desc: Delete current window.

name: describe-bindings
desc: List all global and local keybindings, putting the result in the *help* buffer.

name: describe-key-briefly
desc: Read a key from the keyboard, and look it up in the keymap. Display the name of the function currently bound to the key.

name: diff-buffer-with-file
desc: View the differences between buffer and its associated file.

name: digit-argument
desc: Process a numerical argument for keyboard-invoked functions.

name: dired-jump
desc: Open a dired buffer containing the current buffer's directory location.

name: downcase-region
desc: Set all characters in the region to lower case.

name: downcase-word
desc: Set characters to lower case, starting at the dot, and ending n words away.

name: emacs-version
desc: Return an version string.

name: end-kbd-macro
desc: Stop defining a keyboard macro.

name: end-of-buffer
desc: Move cursor to the end of the buffer. If set, keep mark's position, otherwise set at current position. A numeric argument n will move n/10th of the way from the end.

name: end-of-line
desc: Move cursor to the end of the line.

name: enlarge-window
desc: Enlarge the current window by shrinking either the window above or below it.

name: eval-current-buffer
desc: Evaluate the current buffer as a series of commands. Useful for testing startup files.

name: eval-expression
desc: Get one line from the user, and run it. Useful for testing expressions in startup files.

name: exchange-point-and-mark
desc: Swap the values of "dot" and "mark" in the current window. Return an error if no mark is set.

name: execute-extended-command
desc: Invoke an extended command; i.e. M-x. Call the message line routine to read in the command name and apply autocompletion to it. When it comes back, look the name up in the symbol table and run the command if it is found, passing arguments as necessary. Print an error if there is anything wrong.

name: fill-paragraph
desc: Justify a paragraph, wrapping text at the current fill column.

name: find-file
desc: Select a file for editing. First check if the file can be found in another buffer; if it is there, just switch to that buffer. If the file cannot be found, create a new buffer, read in the file from disk, and switch to the new buffer.

name: find-file-read-only
desc: Same as find-file , except the new buffer is set to read-only.

name: find-alternate-file
desc: Replace the current file with an alternate one. Semantics for finding the replacement file are the same as find-file , except the current buffer is killed before the switch. If the kill fails, or is aborted, revert to the original file.

name: find-file-other-window
desc: Opens the specified file in a second buffer. Splits the current window if necessary.

name: find-tag
desc: Jump to definition of tag at dot.

name: forward-char
desc: Move cursor forwards (or backwards, if n is negative) n characters. Returns an error if the end of buffer is reached.

name: forward-paragraph
desc: Move forward n paragraphs. Paragraphs are delimited by <NL><NL> or <NL><TAB> or <NL><SPACE>.

name: forward-word
desc: Move the cursor forward by the specified number of words.

name: global-set-key
desc: Bind a key in the global (fundamental) key map.

name: global-unset-key
desc: Unbind a key from the global (fundamental) key map; i.e. set it to 'rescan'.

name: global-wd-mode
desc: Toggle global working-directory mode. When enabled, defaults to opening files (and executing commands like compile and grep ) relative to the global working directory. When disabled, a working directory is set for each buffer.

name: goto-line
desc: Go to a specific line. If an argument is present, then it is the line number, else prompt for a line number to use.

name: help-help
desc: Prompts for one of (a)propos, (b)indings, des(c)ribe key briefly.

name: insert
desc: Insert a string, mainly for use from macros.

name: insert-buffer
desc: Insert the contents of another buffer at dot.

name: insert-file
desc: Insert a file into the current buffer at dot.

name: insert-with-wrap
desc: Insert the bound character with word wrap. Check to see if we're past the fill column, and if so, justify this line.

name: isearch-backward
desc: Use incremental searching, initially in the reverse direction. isearch ignores any explicit arguments. If invoked during macro definition or evaluation, the non-incremental search-backward is invoked instead.

name: isearch-forward
desc: Use incremental searching, initially in the forward direction. isearch ignores any explicit arguments. If invoked during macro definition or evaluation, the non-incremental search-forward is invoked instead.

name: join-line
desc: Join the current line to the previous. If called with an argument, join the next line to the current one.

name: just-one-space
desc: Delete any whitespace around dot, then insert a space.

name: keyboard-quit
desc: Abort the current action.

name: kill-buffer
desc: Dispose of a buffer, by name. If the buffer name does not start and end with an asterisk, prompt the user if the buffer has been changed.

name: kill-line
desc: Kill line. If called without an argument, it kills from dot to the end of the line, unless it is at the end of the line, when it kills the newline. If called with an argument of 0, it kills from the start of the line to dot. If called with a positive argument, it kills from dot forward over that number of newlines. If called with a negative argument it kills any text before dot on the current line, then it kills back

name: kill-paragraph
desc: Delete n paragraphs starting with the current one.

name: kill-region
desc: Kill the currently defined region.

name: kill-word
desc: Delete forward n words.

name: leave-tmpdir-backups
desc: Modifies the behaviour of backup-to-home-directory . Backup files that would normally reside in /tmp are left there and not moved to the ~/.mg.d directory.

name: line-number-mode
desc: Toggle whether the line number is displayed in the modeline.

name: list-buffers
desc: Display the list of available buffers. The first column in the output indicates which buffer is active with a '>' character. The second column indicates which buffers are modified. The third column indicates which buffers are read-only. The remaining columns are self-explanatory.

name: load
desc: Prompt the user for a filename, and then execute commands from that file.

name: local-set-key
desc: Bind a key mapping in the local (topmost) mode.

name: local-unset-key
desc: Unbind a key mapping in the local (topmost) mode.

name: make-backup-files
desc: Toggle generation of backup files. Enabled by default.

name: make-directory
desc: Prompt the user for a path or directory name which is then created.

name: mark-paragraph
desc: Mark n paragraphs.

name: mark-whole-buffer
desc: Marks whole buffer as a region by putting dot at the beginning and mark at the end of buffer.

name: meta-key-mode
desc: When disabled, the meta key can be used to insert extended-ascii (8-bit) characters. When enabled, the meta key acts as usual.

name: negative-argument
desc: Process a negative argument for keyboard-invoked functions.

name: newline
desc: Insert a newline into the current buffer.

name: newline-and-indent
desc: Insert a newline, then enough tabs and spaces to duplicate the indentation of the previous line, respecting no-tab-mode and the buffer tab width.

name: next-line
desc: Move forward n lines.

name: no-tab-mode
desc: Toggle notab mode. In this mode, spaces are inserted rather than tabs. Can be set globally with set-default-mode .

name: not-modified
desc: Turn off the modified flag in the current buffer.

name: open-line
desc: Open up some blank space. Essentially, insert n newlines, then back up over them.

name: other-window
desc: The command to make the next (down the screen) window the current window. There are no real errors, although the command does nothing if there is only 1 window on the screen.

name: overwrite-mode
desc: Toggle overwrite mode in the current buffer, where typing overwrites existing characters rather than inserting them. Can be set globally with set-default-mode .

name: prefix-region
desc: Inserts a prefix string before each line of a region. The prefix string is settable by using set-prefix-string or by invoking this command with a prefix argument.

name: previous-line
desc: Move backwards n lines.

name: previous-window
desc: This command makes the previous (up the screen) window the current window. There are no errors, although the command does not do a lot if there is only 1 window.

name: pop-tag-mark
desc: Return to position where find-tag was previously invoked.

name: push-shell
desc: Suspend and switch to alternate screen, if available.

name: pwd
desc: Display current (global) working directory in the status area.

name: query-replace
desc: Query Replace. Search and replace strings selectively, prompting after each match.

name: replace-regexp
desc: Replace regular expression globally without individual prompting.

name: replace-string
desc: Replace string globally without individual prompting.

name: query-replace-regexp
desc: Replace strings selectively. Does a search and replace operation using regular expressions for both patterns.

name: quoted-insert
desc: Insert the next character verbatim into the current buffer; i.e. ignore any function bound to that key.

name: re-search-again
desc: Perform a regular expression search again, using the same search string and direction as the last search command.

name: re-search-backward
desc: Search backwards using a regular expression. Get a search string from the user, and search, starting at dot and proceeding toward the front of the buffer. If found, dot is left pointing at the first character of the pattern [the last character that was matched].

name: re-search-forward
desc: Search forward using a regular expression. Get a search string from the user and search for it starting at dot. If found, move dot to just after the matched characters. display does all the hard stuff. If not found, it just prints a message.

name: recenter
desc: Reposition dot in the current window. By default, the dot is centered. If given a positive argument (n), the display is repositioned to line n. If n is negative, it is that line from the bottom.

name: redraw-display
desc: Refresh the display. Recomputes all window sizes in case something has changed.

name: require-final-newline n
desc: Control whether a newline is added at end of file when saving. n may be -1 to prompt the user (the default), 0 to never add a newline, or 1 to always add one silently.

name: revert-buffer
desc: Revert the current buffer to the latest file on disk.

name: save-buffer
desc: Save the contents of the current buffer if it has been changed, optionally creating a backup copy.

name: save-buffers-kill-emacs
desc: Offer to save modified buffers and quit .

name: save-some-buffers
desc: Look through the list of buffers, offering to save any buffer that has been changed. Buffers that are not associated with files (such as *scratch*, *grep*, *compile*) are ignored.

name: scroll-down
desc: Scroll backwards n pages. A two-line overlap between pages is assumed. If given a repeat argument, scrolls back lines, not pages.

name: scroll-one-line-down
desc: Scroll the display down n lines without changing the cursor position.

name: scroll-one-line-up
desc: Scroll the display n lines up without moving the cursor position.

name: scroll-other-window
desc: Scroll the next window in the window list window forward n pages.

name: scroll-up
desc: Scroll forward one page. A two-line overlap between pages is assumed. If given a repeat argument, scrolls back lines, not pages.

name: search-again
desc: Search again, using the same search string and direction as the last search command.

name: search-backward
desc: Reverse search. Get a search string from the user, and search, starting at dot and proceeding toward the front of the buffer. If found, dot is left pointing at the first character of the pattern (the last character that was matched).

name: search-forward
desc: Search forward. Get a search string from the user, and search for it starting at dot. If found, dot gets moved to just after the matched characters, if not found, print a message.

name: self-insert-command
desc: Insert a character.

name: sentence-end-double-space
desc: Toggle double or single spaces for end of sentences. Double is the default. Currently only affects fill-paragraph.

name: set-case-fold-search
desc: Set case-fold searching, causing case not to matter in regular expression searches. This is the default.

name: set-case-replace
desc: Preserve the case of the replaced string. This is the default.

name: set-default-mode
desc: Append the supplied mode to the list of default modes used by subsequent buffer creation. Built in modes include: fill, indent, notab and overwrite.

name: set-fill-column
desc: Prompt the user for a fill column. Used by auto-fill-mode .

name: set-mark-command
desc: Sets the mark in the current window to the current dot location.

name: set-prefix-string
desc: Sets the prefix string to be used by the prefix-region command.

name: set-tab-width
desc: Set the tab width for the current buffer, or the default for new buffers if called with a prefix argument or from the startup file.

name: shell-command
desc: Execute external command from mini-buffer. With a universal argument it inserts the command output into the current buffer.

name: shell-command-on-region
desc: Provide the text in region to the shell command as input. With a universal argument it replaces the region with the command output.

name: shrink-window
desc: Shrink current window by one line. The window immediately below is expanded to pick up the slack. If only one window is present, this command has no effect.

name: space-to-tabstop
desc: Insert enough spaces to reach the next tab-stop position. By default, tab-stops occur every 8 characters.

name: split-window-vertically
desc: Split the current window. A window smaller than 3 lines cannot be split.

name: start-kbd-macro
desc: Start defining a keyboard macro. Macro definition is ended by invoking end-kbd-macro.

name: suspend-emacs
desc: Suspend and switch back to alternate screen, if in use.

name: switch-to-buffer
desc: Prompt and switch to a new buffer in the current window.

name: switch-to-buffer-other-window
desc: Switch to buffer in another window.

name: toggle-read-only
desc: Toggle the read-only flag on the current buffer.

name: toggle-read-only-all
desc: Toggle the read-only flag on all non-ephemeral buffers. A simple toggle that switches a global read-only flag either on or off.

name: transpose-chars
desc: Transpose the two characters in front of and under dot, then move forward one character. Treat newline characters the same as any other.

name: transpose-paragraphs
desc: Transpose adjacent paragraphs. If multiple iterations are requested, the current paragraph will be moved n paragraphs forward.

name: transpose-words
desc: Transpose adjacent words.

name: undo
desc: Undo the most recent action. If invoked again without an intervening command, move the undo pointer to the previous action and undo it.

name: undo-boundary
desc: Add an undo boundary. This is not usually done interactively.

name: undo-boundary-toggle
desc: Toggle whether undo boundaries are generated. Undo boundaries are often disabled before operations that should be considered atomically undoable.

name: undo-enable
desc: Toggle whether undo information is kept.

name: undo-list
desc: Show the undo records for the current buffer in a new buffer.

name: universal-argument
desc: Repeat the next command 4 times. Usually bound to C-u. This command may be stacked; e.g. C-u C-u C-f moves the cursor forward 16 characters.

name: upcase-region
desc: Upper case region. Change all of the lower case characters in the region to upper case.

name: upcase-word
desc: Move the cursor forward by the specified number of words. As it moves, convert any characters to upper case.

name: visible-bell
desc: Toggle the visible bell. If this toggle is on, the modeline will flash.

name: visit-tags-table
desc: Load tags file to be used for subsequent find-tag .

name: what-cursor-position
desc: Display a bunch of useful information about the current location of dot. The character under the cursor (in octal), the current line, row, and column, and approximate position of the cursor in the file (as a percentage) is displayed. The column position assumes an infinite position display; it does not truncate just because the screen does.

name: write-file
desc: Ask for a file name and write the contents of the current buffer to that file. Update the remembered file name and clear the buffer changed flag.

name: yank
desc: Yank text from kill-buffer . Unlike emacs, the kill buffer consists only of the most recent kill. It is not a ring.

name: zap-to-char
desc: Ask for a character and delete text from the current cursor position until the next instance of that character, including it.

name: zap-up-to-char
desc: Like zap-to-char but doesn't delete the target character.

name: dired-do-flagged-delete
desc: Delete the files that have been flagged for deletion.

name: dired-do-rename
desc: Rename the file listed on the current line of the dired buffer.

name: dired-find-alternate-file
desc: Replace the current dired buffer with an alternate one as specified by the position of the cursor in the dired buffer.

name: dired-find-file
desc: Open the file on the current line of the dired buffer. If the cursor is on a directory, it will be opened in dired mode.

name: dired-flag-file-deletion
desc: Flag the file listed on the current line for deletion. This is indicated in the buffer by putting a D at the left margin. No files are actually deleted until the function dired-do-flagged-delete is executed.

name: dired-find-file-other-window
desc: Open the file on the current line of the dired buffer in a different window.

name: dired-goto-file
desc: Move the cursor to a file name in the dired buffer.

name: dired-next-line
desc: Move the cursor to the next line.

name: dired-other-window
desc: This function works just like dired, except that it puts the dired buffer in another window.

name: dired-previous-line
desc: Move the cursor to the previous line.

name: dired-revert
desc: Refresh the dired buffer while retaining any flags.

name: dired-scroll-down
desc: Scroll down the dired buffer.

name: dired-scroll-up
desc: Scroll up the dired buffer.

name: dired-shell-command
desc: Pipe the file under the current cursor position through a shell command.

name: dired-unmark
desc: Remove the deletion flag for the file on the current line.

name: dired-unmark-backward
desc: Remove the deletion flag from the file listed on the previous line of the dired buffer, then move up to that line.

name: dired-up-directory
desc: Open a dired buffer in the parent directory.

name: quit-window
desc: Close the current dired buffer.
